sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: On any given day, you can find plenty of examples of people doing bad things.
sentences.zh: 在任何一天里，你都能找到大量人们做坏事的例子。

sentences.en: Domestic violence is on the rise.
sentences.zh: 家庭暴力正在增加。

sentences.en: It's early this morning, an 82-year-old man beaten and robbed inside a Lower East Side bodega.
sentences.zh: 今天清晨，一名82岁的老人在下东区的一家小杂货店里遭到殴打和抢劫。

sentences.en: Which could lead to such things as them draining your bank account.
sentences.zh: 这可能会导致他们掏空你的银行账户等后果。

sentences.en: Our two people have been arrested, accused of human trafficking teenagers here in Central Florida.
sentences.zh: 我们有两人被捕，被指控在中佛罗里达州贩卖未成年人。

sentences.en: It makes sense that our attention is drawn to these sorts of people.
sentences.zh: 我们的注意力被这类人吸引，这是合乎情理的。

sentences.en: From an evolutionary perspective, being alert to those who might cause us harm can help to keep us safe.
sentences.zh: 从演化的角度来看，对可能对我们造成伤害的人保持警惕有助于保证我们的安全。

sentences.en: Calling out these people also helps to reinforce the rules of our society.
sentences.zh: 谴责这些人也有助于强化我们社会的规则。

sentences.en: But is it possible that we've become too focused on the wrongdoers amongst us?
sentences.zh: 但我们有没有可能把太多的注意力集中在我们身边的作恶者身上了呢？

sentences.en: What if our focus on the bad makes it harder to see the many good people in our midst?
sentences.zh: 如果我们把注意力放在坏人身上，会不会让我们更难看到我们中间众多的好人呢？

sentences.en: And what happens when these biases play out, not just at an individual level, but are built into the structures of communities and nations?
sentences.zh: 当这些偏见不仅在个人层面发挥作用，而且被构建到社区和国家的结构中时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: In policy-making circles, you are regarded as highly intelligent and realistic if you say,
sentences.zh: 在决策圈子里，如果你这样说，就会被认为非常聪明和现实：

sentences.en: Listen, everybody's selfish.
sentences.zh: 听着，每个人都是自私的。

sentences.en: We have to treat the citizen, the taxpayer, the employee, and so on, as if he or she was entirely selfish.
sentences.zh: 我们必须把公民、纳税人、员工等所有人当作完全自私的人来对待。

sentences.en: Because otherwise, maybe we're a chump or maybe we'll be taken advantage of, and so on.
sentences.zh: 因为否则，也许我们就是个傻瓜，或者我们会被占便宜，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Over the past few weeks, we've looked at how we gauge other people's intentions,
sentences.zh: 在过去的几周里，我们探讨了我们如何衡量别人的意图，

sentences.en: why we underestimate our own likability in interpersonal settings,
sentences.zh: 为什么我们在人际交往中低估了自己的好感度，

sentences.en: and how we often fail to understand our own motivations.
sentences.zh: 以及我们如何经常无法理解自己的动机。

sentences.en: Today, we continue our Mind Reading 2.0 series with a 2020 episode about how we profoundly underestimate the goodness in human nature,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们的“读心术2.0”系列继续播出，这是一期2020年的节目，内容关于我们如何深深地低估了人性的善良，

sentences.en: and how this era is woven into the fabric of our societies.
sentences.zh: 以及这种观念是如何融入我们社会结构中的。

sentences.en: What we lose when we assume people are bad.
sentences.zh: 当我们假设人们是坏的时，我们会失去什么。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Both in times of crisis and in normal times, public policy is focused on keeping bad people from doing bad things.
sentences.zh: 无论是危机时期还是平常时期，公共政策的重点都是阻止坏人做坏事。

sentences.en: Behavioral economist Sam Bowles thinks this is a mistake.
sentences.zh: 行为经济学家萨姆·鲍尔斯认为这是一个错误。

sentences.en: He worries that such policies not only underestimate the capacity of most people to do the right thing,
sentences.zh: 他担心，此类政策不仅低估了大多数人做正确事情的能力，

sentences.en: but can inadvertently hurt our ability to do right by others.
sentences.zh: 而且还可能无意中损害我们为他人做正确之举的能力。

sentences.en: He explores this idea in his book, The Moral Economy.
sentences.zh: 他在其著作《道德经济学》中探讨了这个观点。

sentences.en: Sam Bowles, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 萨姆·鲍尔斯，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thanks very much, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: A central assumption in economics, Sam, is that humans are motivated by rational self-intereSt.
sentences.zh: 萨姆，经济学的一个核心假设是，人类的动机是理性的自我利益。

sentences.en: The price of something goes up, I buy less of it, the price of something goes down, I buy more of it.
sentences.zh: 某种东西价格上涨，我少买一点；某种东西价格下降，我多买一点。

sentences.en: Like many behavioral economists, you say this assumption turns our species of Homo sapiens into a new one, Homo economicus.
sentences.zh: 像许多行为经济学家一样，你说这个假设把我们智人这个物种变成了一个新物种——经济人。

sentences.en: What are the traits of this other species?
sentences.zh: 这个新物种有什么特征？

sentences.en: Well, this being, Homo economicus or economic man, cares only about himself or herself,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个生物，也就是“经济人”，只关心他自己或她自己，

sentences.en: and therefore evaluates actions that may be taken simply in terms of what's in it for me.
sentences.zh: 因此，他对可能采取的行动的评估，仅仅从“对我有什么好处”的角度出发。

sentences.en: That's the basic idea of Homo economicus.
sentences.zh: 这就是经济人的基本理念。

sentences.en: So that's the self-interest part.
sentences.zh: 所以这是自私的那一部分。

sentences.en: Now, there's another part, which is that we're, not only are we self-interested, we're pretty good at doing it.
sentences.zh: 现在，还有另一部分，那就是我们不仅自私，而且在这方面做得相当好。

sentences.en: So we're very able to think about the consequences of our actions.
sentences.zh: 所以我们非常有能力思考我们行动的后果。

sentences.en: And that's the part that usually is associated with the word rational.
sentences.zh: 这就是通常与“理性”一词相关的部分。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I'm wondering how this idea has percolated beyond the boundaries of just economics.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这个想法是如何渗透到经济学边界之外的。

sentences.en: Because I feel like when I watch television or read books, this idea that people are out for themselves, you see this everywhere.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得当我看电视或读书时，这种“人们都是为了自己”的想法随处可见。

sentences.en: I'm thinking about the TV show Succession, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如我想到了电视剧《继承之战》。

sentences.en: I'm concerned you might be soft.
sentences.zh: 我担心你可能会心软。

sentences.en: The only way he'll respect you is if you try to destroy him.
sentences.zh: 他尊重你的唯一方法就是你试图摧毁他。

sentences.en: I'm not saying I would make a better CEO.
sentences.zh: 我不是说我会成为一个更好的CEO。

sentences.en: That's unsaid.
sentences.zh: 这是不言而喻的。

sentences.en: It's not unsaid when you say it.
sentences.zh: 当你把它说出来时，这就不是不言而喻了。

sentences.en: You know, all the members of this family are fighting tooth and nail to take over their father's media company.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这个家族的所有成员都在拼命争夺他们父亲的传媒公司。

sentences.en: No one trusts each other.
sentences.zh: 没有人信任彼此。

sentences.en: Everyone is out for only one thing, which is personal gain.
sentences.zh: 每个人都只有一个目的，那就是个人利益。

sentences.en: So this idea that rational behavior is selfish behavior is more than just economics right now.
sentences.zh: 所以，理性行为就是自私行为这一观点，现在已经不仅仅局限于经济学。

sentences.en: It's in pop culture.
sentences.zh: 它存在于流行文化中。

sentences.en: It's in books.
sentences.zh: 它存在于书籍中。

sentences.en: It's in movies, not just in textbooks.
sentences.zh: 它存在于电影中，而不仅仅是教科书中。

sentences.en: I think that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 我认为完全正确。

sentences.en: There is the economics of the classroom, the seminar room, and the think tank.
sentences.zh: 存在课堂、研讨会和智库的经济学。

sentences.en: And that's presented in a certain way, usually fairly mathematically and so on.
sentences.zh: 这以某种方式呈现，通常相当数学化等等。

sentences.en: But then there's what I call the economics vernacular.
sentences.zh: 但还有我所说的经济学白话。

sentences.en: That's the way ordinary people express economic truths.
sentences.zh: 那是普通人表达经济真理的方式。

sentences.en: And what you'll hear a lot is you get what you pay for.
sentences.zh: 你会经常听到“一分钱一分货”。

sentences.en: Or you'll hear former British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher saying there's no such thing as society.
sentences.zh: 或者你会听到英国前首相玛格丽特·撒切尔说根本没有社会这回事。

sentences.en: All we are is an individual.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人不过是个人。

sentences.en: And these then become common sayings.
sentences.zh: 这些后来都成了俗语。

sentences.en: So I want to talk about one last domain before we switch to some of the problems with the model that you and others have identified.
sentences.zh: 所以我想讨论最后一个领域，然后我们再转入你和他人所指出的该模型的某些问题。

sentences.en: It's not just in pop culture and it's not just in business and in commerce.
sentences.zh: 它不仅存在于流行文化中，也不仅存在于商业和贸易中。

sentences.en: If you think that human beings are fundamentally motivated by self-interest, by narrow self-interest, by selfishness,
sentences.zh: 如果你认为人类的根本动机是自私利益，是狭隘的自私利益，是自私，

sentences.en: then if you're a government, your job as the government is to try and restrict how people behave,
sentences.zh: 那么如果你是政府，你作为政府的工作就是尝试限制人们的行为，

sentences.zh: 你想要给人们的自私踩刹车。

sentences.en: because that's all the people who are out there.
sentences.zh: 因为外面的所有人都是这样。

sentences.en: They're all knaves and villains.
sentences.zh: 他们全都是无赖和恶棍。

sentences.en: Well, that's exactly what some governments have done.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这正是某些政府所做的。

sentences.en: And I think one of the really remarkable things is that in policymaking circles,
sentences.zh: 我认为真正引人注目的一点是，在决策圈子里，

sentences.en: as if he or she was entirely selfish because otherwise maybe we're a chump or maybe we'll be taken advantage of and so on.
sentences.zh: 当作完全自私的人来对待，因为否则也许我们是个傻瓜，或者我们会被占便宜，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So people who don't really believe it think that you should go on with this assumption of homo economicus
sentences.zh: 所以那些并不是真正相信这一点的人认为，你应该继续秉持这种经济人的假设，

sentences.en: because it's prudent.
sentences.zh: 因为这是审慎的。

sentences.en: There might be some people who are really like that and if so, we'd better watch out
sentences.zh: 可能确实有一些人真的是那样，如果是这样，我们最好小心防范，

sentences.en: and therefore we're going to design policies and so on as if everyone was that way.
sentences.zh: 因此我们要设计政策等等，就好像每个人都是那样的人一样。

sentences.en: David Hume, a philosopher economist of the 18th century, just before Adam Smith,
sentences.zh: 大卫·休谟，18世纪的哲学家兼经济学家，就在亚当·斯密之前，

sentences.en: he said that in designing a government, you should assume that everyone is a knave.
sentences.zh: 他说过，在设计政府时，你应该假设每个人都是无赖。

sentences.en: He used that ancient word, a knave, and has nothing in his mind but pursuing his own intereSt.
sentences.zh: 他用了那个古老的词“无赖”，其心中所想唯有追求自己的利益。

sentences.en: So given the predominance of the standard economic model, homo economicus,
sentences.zh: 鉴于标准经济模型（经济人）的主导地位，

sentences.en: not just in economics but in politics and popular culture and other domains,
sentences.zh: 不仅在经济学中，而且在政治、流行文化和其他领域中，

sentences.en: it's interesting that the models have trouble explaining why people do lots of things.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这些模型很难解释为什么人们会做很多事情。

sentences.en: And the classic example that's often given is that you're on a trip to a foreign country,
sentences.zh: 经常给出的经典例子是，你到外国旅行，

sentences.zh: 你去了一家餐馆，在餐馆坐下，吃了一顿美餐，

sentences.en: And you're never going to see the waiter again because you're probably not going to go back
sentences.zh: 你再也不会见到这个服务员了，因为你大概这辈子都不会再去了

sentences.en: The rational, self-interested thing to do is to save some of your money.

sentences.en: But many of us don't.

sentences.en: We decide to tip that waiter anyway.

sentences.en: And maybe some of it is habit or maybe it's guilt.

sentences.en: Maybe it just makes you feel good.
sentences.zh: 也许这只是让你感觉良好。

sentences.en: Whatever the reason, there's all this messy human stuff that seems to live outside the model

sentences.zh: 令我惊讶的是，经济学家没有比现在更早地去想：

sentences.en: And there are other things having to do with feelings, obligations, and so on.
sentences.zh: 而还有其他部分负责处理情感、责任等等。

sentences.en: But the fact that just putting some money on the table will relocate the activity of the
sentences.zh: 但仅仅把一些金钱摆在台面上，就会将大脑的活动

sentences.en: brain to the prefrontal cortex, which is where you process benefits and costs and so on,
sentences.zh: 重新定位到前额叶皮层——也就是处理成本和效益等事物的地方，

sentences.en: is really a striking finding.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个惊人的发现。

sentences.en: So it suggests that, you know, that's what we're like.
sentences.zh: 这表明，你知道，这就是我们的天性。

sentences.en: And we're probably not going to change, so we'd better accommodate that.
sentences.zh: 而且我们大概不会改变，所以我们最好顺应这一点。

sentences.en: One of the sad things you note about the Haifa daycare story is what happened when the daycare
sentences.zh: 关于海法日托中心的故事，令人遗憾的一点是，当该中心

sentences.en: reversed the policy around the fines.
sentences.zh: 取消了罚款政策时，情况发生了变化。

sentences.en: So obviously it backfired, and then administrators reversed the policy and said,
sentences.zh: 显然，这适得其反，于是管理者取消了政策并表示：

sentences.en: OK, we're taking away the fines.
sentences.zh: “好吧，我们取消罚款。”

sentences.en: What happened afterwards, Sam?
sentences.zh: 后来发生了什么，山姆？

sentences.en: That's an amazing thing.
sentences.zh: 那真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: When they took away the fine, the lateness persisted in the schools, in the daycare centers,
sentences.zh: 当他们取消罚款后，迟到现象在那些

sentences.en: which had had the fine.
sentences.zh: 曾实行过罚款的学校和日托中心里依然存在。

sentences.en: The control schools, the control centers had no effect.
sentences.zh: 而对照学校和对照中心则没有受到影响。

sentences.en: But now, just to get this, I have to say it again because it's so unusual.
sentences.zh: 但为了弄明白这一点，我必须再说一遍，因为它太不寻常了。

sentences.en: When they imposed the fine on being late, the parents came later.
sentences.zh: 当他们对迟到处以罚款时，家长们反而来得更晚了。

sentences.en: And when they took away the fine, they continued coming later.
sentences.zh: 而当他们取消罚款时，家长们依然继续迟到。

sentences.en: Well, why is that?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, I think the story about framing is exactly what happened.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为关于框架效应的解释正好说明了发生的事情。

sentences.en: It used to be an ethical question.
sentences.zh: 过去，这是一个道德问题。

sentences.en: You should come on time.
sentences.zh: 你应该按时到达。

sentences.en: They tried to.
sentences.zh: 他们尽量做到。

sentences.en: Sometimes they didn't.
sentences.zh: 有时他们没做到。

sentences.en: Once it became just a matter of step right up and purchase a little lateness if you want,
sentences.zh: 一旦这变成了一件“如果你愿意，尽管上前买一点迟到时间”的事情，

sentences.en: that didn't change.
sentences.zh: 情况就没有改变。

sentences.en: After they took the fine away, it still seemed to them that they had already been told,
sentences.zh: 在他们取消罚款后，家长们仍然觉得他们之前已经被告知过，

sentences.en: oh, this is something I can buy.
sentences.zh: 哦，这是我可以花钱买的东西。

sentences.en: And only now I can buy it for free because for some reason they took away the price.
sentences.zh: 而且现在我可以免费购买了，因为不知为什么他们取消了价格。

sentences.en: I'm wondering whether you might have friends in the economics department who might say
sentences.zh: 我在想，你经济学系的朋友可能会说：

sentences.en: the problem with Haifa was not that they introduced fines, but that the fines were not big enough,
sentences.zh: 海法的问题不在于他们引入了罚款，而在于罚款不够高，

sentences.en: that in some ways the incentive was not strong enough.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，激励力度还不够强。

sentences.en: If you had actually made it instead of 10 shekels, if you had made it 200,
sentences.zh: 如果你实际上不设为 10 谢克尔，而是设为 200 谢克尔，

sentences.en: everyone would have come on time because at that point no one thinks 15 minutes is worth 200 shekels.
sentences.zh: 所有人都会按时到达，因为到那个时候，没人会觉得 15 分钟值 200 谢克尔。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很有道理。

sentences.en: I think that objection is perfectly sound, that there is some level of monetary incentive
sentences.zh: 我认为这种反驳完全合情合理，即确实存在某种水平的货币激励，

sentences.en: which will lead people to conform to the rules.
sentences.zh: 会引导人们遵守规则。

sentences.en: It just means that because they're ethical and because you start out by crowding out
sentences.zh: 但这只是意味着，由于他们本身具有道德感，而你从一开始就排挤了

sentences.en: the ethical motivation, which was the reason why they were coming on time, most of them,
sentences.zh: 他们的道德动机——而这正是他们大多数人原本按时到达的原因，

sentences.en: in the first place.
sentences.zh: 一开始就是这样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So you start basically in the hole by having destroyed what Adam Smith called moral sentiments.
sentences.zh: 所以，由于你摧毁了亚当·斯密所谓的道德情感，你基本上从一开始就处于劣势。

sentences.en: Now, the fact that you can make up for it by a large fine or severe penalties, of course you can do that.
sentences.zh: 当然，你可以通过巨额罚款或严厉惩罚来弥补这一点，你完全可以这样做。

sentences.en: It's not clear that we want to live in a society which has fines of enormous amounts and so on
sentences.zh: 但并不清楚我们是否愿意生活在一个拥有巨额罚款等机制的社会中，

sentences.en: or other kinds of penalties, particularly when we can find ways of mobilizing people's desire
sentences.zh: 或者其他类型的惩罚，特别是当我们能够找到方法去调动人们的愿望时——

sentences.en: to be a good citizen, to be good to their neighbors, to be considerate of their teachers and so on.
sentences.zh: 即渴望成为好公民、善待邻居、体谅老师等等的愿望。

sentences.en: Many of us would probably agree that we'd like to live in a society that encourages our desire to be good
sentences.zh: 我们当中的许多人可能会认同，我们更愿意生活在一个鼓励我们向善的愿望的社会里，

sentences.en: rather than one that assumes we're going to be bad.
sentences.zh: 而不是一个假设我们会作恶的社会。

sentences.en: The question is, how do we begin to get there?
sentences.zh: 问题是，我们如何才能开始实现这一点？

sentences.en: In Ireland, they said, look, this is a serious problem for us.
sentences.zh: 在爱尔兰，他们说：看，这对我们来说是个严重的问题。

sentences.en: We're trashing our country and let's stop doing it.
sentences.zh: 我们正在糟蹋我们的国家，让我们别再这么做了。

sentences.en: That's when we come back.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们要回归的话题。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: One of the core assumptions of economics is that we will behave in ways that serve our individual needs.
sentences.zh: 经济学的核心假设之一是，我们的行为将服务于个人的需求。

sentences.en: In other words, we'll act in our rational self-intereSt.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们会出于理性的自利心理行事。

sentences.en: You don't need to be an economist, however, to know that people are not purely self-interested.
sentences.zh: 然而，你不需要成为一名经济学家，就知道人们并非完全出于自私。

sentences.en: Most of us follow the rules, even when it's unlikely that we'll get caught breaking them.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人都会遵守规则，即使不太可能因违规而被抓。

sentences.en: We give money to charity, even when such donations do not benefit us directly.
sentences.zh: 我们会向慈善机构捐款，即使这些捐款并不能直接让我们受益。

sentences.en: Every day, people show a desire to behave generously and to help the common good.
sentences.zh: 每天，人们都表现出慷慨行为和促进共同利益的愿望。

sentences.en: Yet very often, in our private lives and in the way we structure societal rules,
sentences.zh: 然而在我们的私生活中，以及在我们构建社会规则的方式中，往往非常频繁地

sentences.en: we fail to recognize these positive aspects of human behavior and how we could do more to foster them.
sentences.zh: 忽视了人类行为这些积极的方面，以及我们本可以采取更多措施来培养这些品质。

sentences.en: Sam Bowles is a behavioral economist at the Santa Fe Institute.
sentences.zh: 山姆·鲍尔斯是圣菲研究所的一位行为经济学家。

sentences.en: He makes the case that our public policy is weighted too much toward keeping bad people from doing bad things.
sentences.zh: 他提出，我们的公共政策在很大程度上偏向于阻止坏人做坏事。

sentences.en: Sam, you've actually mentioned a phrase a couple of times in our conversation, and it has to do with this idea of crowding out and crowding in.
sentences.zh: 山姆，在我们的对话中，你实际上已经多次提到过一个词组，它与排挤效应和引入效应这一概念有关。

sentences.en: I want to spend a moment talking about this idea.
sentences.zh: 我想花一点时间来探讨这个想法。

sentences.en: People do things for lots of reasons.
sentences.zh: 人们出于多种原因做事。

sentences.en: Sometimes they're driven by money, sometimes by pride, sometimes by habit.
sentences.zh: 有时他们受金钱驱使，有时受自豪感驱动，有时则出于习惯。

sentences.en: But when you make them focus on one or the other of these drivers, it can crowd out the other drivers.
sentences.zh: 但当你让他们专注于其中某一种驱动力时，它就会排挤掉其他的驱动力。

sentences.en: You tell a wonderful story about your own kids.
sentences.zh: 你讲过一个关于你自己的孩子的精彩故事。

sentences.en: You wanted to incentivize them to do some household chores, and you turn to mainstream economics for advice.
sentences.zh: 你希望激励他们做一些家务，于是你向主流经济学寻求建议。

sentences.en: Can you tell me the story of what happened and what you mean by this phrase, crowding in, crowding out?
sentences.zh: 你能给我讲讲当时发生了什么，以及你所说的“引入效应”和“排挤效应”是什么意思吗？

sentences.en: Well, the story is about me, and it's even worse than you say.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个故事是关于我自己的，而且比你说的还要糟糕。

sentences.en: My kids were very helpful around the house, and they did a lot.
sentences.zh: 我的孩子们在家里非常乐于助人，他们做了很多事。

sentences.en: I was a single dad, and they were great.
sentences.zh: 我是一个单亲爸爸，他们非常棒。

sentences.en: And as they became teenagers, they began to want to buy clothes and a lot of things like that.
sentences.zh: 随着他们变成青少年，他们开始想要买衣服和许多诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: And I thought, well, you know, a good way to accommodate this is that instead of them just doing stuff around the house, cleaning dishes and helping me in lots of ways,
sentences.zh: 我想，嗯，你知道，适应这种需求的一个好方法是，与其让他们只是在家里帮忙、洗碗并以各种方式协助我，

sentences.en: I would issue a price liSt.
sentences.zh: 不如我发布一份价目表。

sentences.en: And then they could get paid for the stuff that they used to do for free.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就可以为他们以前免费做的事情获得报酬。

sentences.en: And, of course, I thought it was a brilliant idea.
sentences.zh: 当然，我当时觉得这是一个绝妙的主意。

sentences.en: And we agreed on the price liSt.
sentences.zh: 我们商定了价目表。

sentences.en: It seemed reasonable.
sentences.zh: 这看起来很合理。

sentences.en: I posted it on the fridge.
sentences.zh: 我把它贴在了冰箱上。

sentences.en: And what happened?
sentences.zh: 然后发生了什么？

sentences.en: Nothing.
sentences.zh: 什么都没有。

sentences.en: Nothing.
sentences.zh: 什么都没有。

sentences.en: They stopped work entirely.
sentences.zh: 他们彻底停工了。

sentences.en: They didn't do a thing.
sentences.zh: 他们什么也没干。

sentences.en: And they were not selfish, because, as I say, they'd been helping me a lot, doing a lot of work.
sentences.zh: 而且他们并非自私，因为正如我所说，他们以前一直在帮我很多忙，做了大量的工作。

sentences.en: But once it was for pay, it didn't seem to be the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但一旦变成了有偿劳动，感觉就完全不一样了。

sentences.en: Now, it's true that, you know, when a particular item they wanted to buy, well, then they might do the lawn.
sentences.zh: 现在，确实，你知道的，当他们想买某个特定的东西时，好吧，他们可能会去修剪草坪。

sentences.en: But they ended up doing much less than before.
sentences.zh: 但他们最终做的事比以前少多了。

sentences.en: And I had to bring the thing to a halt and say, let's go back to just us doing stuff together.
sentences.zh: 我不得不叫停这件事并说：让我们回到以前那种一起做事的状态吧。

sentences.en: Now, I wonder if your listeners are thinking, oh, my God, those poor kids having an economist for a dad.
sentences.zh: 现在，我在想，你的听众是否在想：天哪，那些可怜的孩子竟然有一个经济学家当爸爸。

sentences.en: And I think there probably is a lot wrong with having an economist for a dad.
sentences.zh: 我想有一个经济学家当爸爸大概确实有很多不好的地方。

sentences.en: And I talked to the kids about it.
sentences.zh: 我和孩子们谈过这件事。

sentences.en: They didn't really have a good explanation of what happened.
sentences.zh: 他们其实也说不出到底发生了什么好解释。

sentences.en: But looking back on it now, I think what happened was this.
sentences.zh: 但现在回想起来，我认为发生的事情是这样的。

sentences.en: They actually enjoyed doing stuff together around the house, and they kind of thought they should help me out.
sentences.zh: 他们其实很喜欢一起在家做事，并且觉得他们应该帮我一把。

sentences.en: They didn't want to see me doing all the stuff by myself.
sentences.zh: 他们不想看到我一个人包揽所有的活。

sentences.en: And so it was something that they both enjoyed intrinsically and felt some obligation to do.
sentences.zh: 所以这是他们发自内心喜欢并觉得有义务去做的事情。

sentences.en: But when I offered to pay them for it, it made them think differently about it, and it made it a matter of choice.
sentences.zh: 但当我提出为此付钱给他们时，这让他们对这件事有了不同的看法，并把它变成了一种选择。

sentences.en: So I think I made the mistake that Adam Smith never made, which is to treat the moral sentiments, that is, the ideas of value contributing to others and so on,
sentences.zh: 所以我想我犯了一个亚当·斯密从未犯过的错误，那就是把道德情感——也就是说，为他人做出价值贡献等观念——

sentences.en: to treat them as if they're somehow separate from or just additive to the incentives that come from material interests and money.
sentences.zh: 当作某种独立于物质利益和金钱所带来的激励，或者仅仅是与之相加的东西来对待。

sentences.en: Sam's incentives demotivated his daughters, but it didn't have to be this way.
sentences.zh: 山姆的激励措施削弱了他女儿们的积极性，但本来不必如此。

sentences.en: You can design incentives to work with the intrinsic pride and satisfaction that people take in doing the right thing.
sentences.zh: 你可以设计激励措施，使其与人们在做正确事情时所获得的内在自豪感和满足感相配合。

sentences.en: Designed effectively, Sam says incentives can amplify, or crowd in, such motives.
sentences.zh: 山姆表示，如果设计得当，激励措施可以放大或引入这种动机。

sentences.en: In Ireland in 2002, for example, the government wanted to reduce the number of plastic bags that people were using.
sentences.zh: 例如，在 2002 年的爱尔兰，政府希望减少人们使用的塑料袋数量。

sentences.en: They came up with an incentive, but first, made an appeal to national pride.
sentences.zh: 他们想出了一种激励措施，但首先，他们呼吁了民族自豪感。

sentences.en: It was preceded by a big campaign about how these bags were so ugly, and Ireland was beautiful, and there was an advertising campaign,
sentences.zh: 在此之前开展了一场大型宣传活动，宣传这些袋子有多么丑陋，而爱尔兰是美丽的，还有一个广告宣传活动，

sentences.en: don't trash the Emerald Isle, and things like that.
sentences.zh: 不要糟蹋翡翠绿岛，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And then this thing was introduced.
sentences.zh: 然后这项措施就被推出了。

sentences.en: It was a very small additional coSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一笔非常小的额外成本。

sentences.en: And within two weeks, the use of plastic bags for shopping was almost completely eliminated.
sentences.zh: 而在两周内，购物时塑料袋的使用几乎被完全消除了。

sentences.en: Now, think about it.
sentences.zh: 现在，仔细想想。

sentences.en: That case was very much like the parents who, when fined, came later instead of shaping up and coming earlier.
sentences.zh: 那个案例非常类似于那些家长：受到罚款时，他们没有改正并提早来，反而来得更晚了。

sentences.en: In Ireland, when you had to pay for using a plastic grocery bag, they stopped using them.
sentences.zh: 在爱尔兰，当你必须为使用塑料购物袋付费时，他们就停止使用了。

sentences.en: And so we have something to learn from that case.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们可以从那个案例中吸取一些经验。

sentences.en: Why is that different from the daycare case?
sentences.zh: 为什么这与日托中心的案例不同？

sentences.en: Because the results were the opposite.
sentences.zh: 因为结果截然相反。

sentences.en: Let's just think about it.
sentences.zh: 让我们仔细想想。

sentences.en: If you pick up your kid at the daycare late, you're one of the very few people who's late.
sentences.zh: 如果你去日托中心接孩子迟到了，你其实是极少数迟到的人之一。

sentences.en: The only other people who see you there being late are other parents picking up their kids late, other than the teacher and your kids.
sentences.zh: 除了老师和你的孩子之外，唯一看到你在那里迟到的人，是其他同样来晚了接孩子的家长。

sentences.en: So, okay, no problem there.
sentences.zh: 所以，好吧，那没什么问题。

sentences.en: They didn't explain why they were doing the fine.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有解释为什么要实行罚款。

sentences.en: They didn't provide any explanation for why they actually should try to discourage lateness.
sentences.zh: 他们没有提供任何解释，说明为什么实际上应该努力减少迟到现象。

sentences.en: In Ireland, it was quite the opposite.
sentences.zh: 而在爱尔兰，情况完全相反。

sentences.en: You're waiting in line, and the person says, do you want some plastic bags?
sentences.zh: 你正在排队，收银员问：你需要塑料袋吗？

sentences.en: And you have to say yes or no.
sentences.zh: 而你必须回答是或否。

sentences.en: And there's three or four or five, six other people there standing there, and they're looking on, and presumably from what happened with disapproval.
sentences.zh: 旁边还有三、四、五个甚至六个人站在那里，他们看着你，根据发生的情况，他们大概带着不赞成的目光。

sentences.en: So it's a very public thing, and you have to choose to do it.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一件非常公开的事情，你必须做出选择。

sentences.en: Arriving late at the daycare, you didn't even know that it was your choice, because, I mean, maybe it really was traffic,
sentences.zh: 迟到去接孩子时，你甚至不知道这是你自己的选择，因为，我的意思是，也许真的是交通堵塞，

sentences.en: rather than deciding to have an extra cup of coffee with a friend.
sentences.zh: 而不是决定和朋友多喝一杯咖啡。

sentences.en: But the other thing which I'm sure was important was, in Ireland, they said, look, this is a serious problem for us.
sentences.zh: 但另一件可以肯定很重要的事是，在爱尔兰，他们说：看，这对我们来说是一个严重的问题。

sentences.en: We're trashing our country, and let's stop doing it.
sentences.zh: 我们在糟蹋我们的国家，让我们别再这么做了。

sentences.en: Let us stop doing it.
sentences.zh: 让我们别再这样做了。

sentences.en: And so I'd like us to learn from the cases where we have crowding in.
sentences.zh: 因此，我想让我们从道德挤入的案例中吸取教训。

sentences.en: Crowding in meaning where the monetary side of the incentive or the side of the package enforces and increases the salience of the moral part.
sentences.zh: 挤入是指，激励的货币方面或整个方案增强了道德部分的显著性。

sentences.en: You know, when we think about the people who make the rules, we think of CEOs, we think of presidents, we think of parents.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们想到制定规则的人时，我们会想到首席执行官、总统和父母。

sentences.en: You know, when these people try to shape the behavior of the people they control with sometimes with the incentives that you described, things can sometimes backfire.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当这些人试图用你有时所描述的激励措施来塑造他们所控制的人的行为时，事情有时会适得其反。

sentences.en: But I can also see this happening in the other direction.
sentences.zh: 但我也可以看到这种情况朝另一个方向发展。

sentences.en: You know, when workers are suspicious that managers are trying to exploit them, they might try to get every single thing written out in a contract about overtime, about sick time,
sentences.zh: 你知道，当工人们怀疑管理者试图剥削他们时，他们可能会试图把合同中关于加班、病假的每一件小事都写清楚，

sentences.en: about all kinds of restrictions about who can work when and in what capacity.
sentences.zh: 关于谁能在什么时候以及以何种身份工作的各种限制。

sentences.en: When citizens are worried that politicians are corrupt, they come up with all kinds of mechanisms to constrain them, term limits and campaign finance limits and various other,
sentences.zh: 当公民担心政客腐败时，他们会想出各种机制来限制他们，比如任期限制、竞选资金限制以及各种其他，

sentences.en: you know, oversight mechanisMs.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，监督机制。

sentences.en: You know, when you signal to a manager or an elected representative or even to a parent that you think they're untrustworthy or corrupt,
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你向管理者、民选代表甚至父母发出信号，表明你认为他们不可信或腐败时，

sentences.en: I'm wondering how do you think that changes the behavior of the people who are in charge?
sentences.zh: 我在想，你认为这会如何改变掌权者的行为？

sentences.en: Well, I think that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为完全是这样。

sentences.en: The signals go in both directions and it's very destructive.
sentences.zh: 这些信号是双向的，而且极具破坏性。

sentences.en: Now, in the case of workers who don't trust the management and owners of a company, therefore insisting on a very detailed contract, that's, in almost all cases,
sentences.zh: 现在，对于那些不信任公司管理层和所有者、因此坚持要有一份非常详细的合同的工人来说，在几乎所有情况下，

sentences.en: self-defeating because there's no way that the contract can cover every possible eventuality.
sentences.zh: 这都是适得其反的，因为合同不可能涵盖所有可能的情况。

sentences.en: And so that's this false hope that if we could just make the contracts complete, cover everything, then we wouldn't care about the other guy.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一种虚假的希望：如果我们能让合同做到面面俱到、包罗万象，那么我们就不必在意另一个人了。

sentences.en: On the other side, he can be as much of a jerk as we want because if we don't get what we're supposed to get, we just basically call the cops, go to court.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，他想怎么混蛋就怎么混蛋，因为如果我们得不到应得的东西，我们基本上就会报警、上法庭。

sentences.en: Now, that's a false hope.
sentences.zh: 现在，这是一种虚假的希望。

sentences.en: But imagine that you're in a situation of management in which you're finding that the people who are working under you are asking you to put everything down on paper,
sentences.zh: 但想象一下，你处于管理者的立场，发现手下的人要求你把所有事情都落实在纸面上，

sentences.en: every single thing.
sentences.zh: 每一件小事。

sentences.en: Well, you know it's not going to work, but you also know that they don't trust you.
sentences.zh: 你知道这行不通，但你也知道他们不信任你。

sentences.en: And so obviously then you would, I think an obvious reaction to that would be to adopt at least defensive and possibly also hostile reaction.
sentences.zh: 很显然，我想对此的一个明显反应就是采取至少是防御性的、甚至可能是敌对的反应。

sentences.en: Researchers and policymakers have long debated many of the ideas we've discussed today.
sentences.zh: 研究人员和政策制定者长期以来一直在争论我们今天讨论的许多观点。

sentences.en: How can we foster trust in our workplaces and in our communities?
sentences.zh: 我们如何在工作场所和社区中培养信任？

sentences.en: What's the best way to incentivize someone to do something they might otherwise decline to do?
sentences.zh: 激励某人去做他们原本可能拒绝的事情的最佳方式是什么？

sentences.en: There are also the sorts of questions that have taken on new urgency during the COVID-19 pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这也是在 COVID-19 大流行期间变得具有新紧迫性的种种问题。

sentences.en: I asked Sam whether he thought the pandemic would give us a way to think afresh about incentives and about the human capacity to do the right thing, even when it's difficult to do.
sentences.zh: 我问萨姆，他是否认为这场大流行病能让我们以崭新的视角来看待激励机制，以及人类在困难时做正确事情的能力。

sentences.en: I think COVID-19 is going to change the way we think about economics and the way we talk about it.
sentences.zh: 我认为 COVID-19 将改变我们思考经济学的方式以及我们谈论经济学的方式。

sentences.en: I think, for example, individualism and self-interest have definitely gotten a bad name over the past, over the duration of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 例如，我认为在疫情期间，个人主义和自利绝对背上了坏名声。

sentences.en: And I think we're going to be rethinking the value of values.
sentences.zh: 我想我们将重新思考价值的价值。

sentences.en: That is, the value of ethical values as an important part of how you organize a society.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，道德价值观作为组织社会的重要组成部分的价值。

sentences.en: So we need to have governments that are trusted by their people.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们需要拥有受人民信任的政府。

sentences.en: We need people who trust the scientific advice of governments.
sentences.zh: 我们需要信任政府科学建议的人民。

sentences.en: And we need people willing to help each other.
sentences.zh: 我们需要愿意互相帮助的人。

sentences.en: So I think we're going to learn some good lessons,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们将吸取一些好的教训，

sentences.en: which is simply relying on self-interest in markets and in relations with government isn't going to be a good way to organize the future.
sentences.zh: 那就是仅仅依靠市场中的自利以及与政府的关系，并不是组织未来的好方法。

sentences.en: COVID tells us that.
sentences.zh: 新冠肺炎疫情告诉了我们这一点。

sentences.en: We have to rely on other things, communities, neighborhoods, obligations we have to each other which are not self-interested.
sentences.zh: 我们必须依靠其他事物：社区、街区、我们对彼此负有的并非出于自利的义务。

sentences.en: That's what we're seeing is fundamentally getting people through this.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们所看到的从根本上让人度过难关的东西。

sentences.en: Now, of course, the market is very important.
sentences.zh: 当然，市场非常重要。

sentences.en: For example, the market is very important in providing incentives, which will be very essential to the distribution,
sentences.zh: 例如，市场在提供激励方面非常重要，这对于疫苗以及其他治疗方法（包括口罩等）的分配、

sentences.en: production and distribution of a vaccine and of other treatments, including masks and so on.
sentences.zh: 生产和分发至关重要。

sentences.en: Governments are essential.
sentences.zh: 政府是必不可少的。

sentences.en: I'm not suggesting that the government and the governments in the market are irrelevant.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说政府以及市场中的政府是不相关的。

sentences.en: What I'm suggesting is that there should be a third dimension of thinking, talking and policymaking.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，应该有第三个维度的思考、对话和决策。

sentences.en: And that's what I would call community or civil society.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所说的社区或公民社会。

sentences.en: The things which are not governmental, but they're not markets either.
sentences.zh: 那些既非政府所有、也非市场所有的事物。

sentences.en: For example, think about social distancing.
sentences.zh: 例如，想想社交距离。

sentences.en: Is that a market phenomenon?
sentences.zh: 这是一种市场现象吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: Well, is it a government phenomenon?
sentences.zh: 那么，这是一种政府现象吗？

sentences.en: Well, the government requires it in some places, but it could never enforce it.
sentences.zh: 政府在某些地方确实有此要求，但它永远无法强制执行。

sentences.en: So, what I hope we're going to learn from this is that you have to rely on people's values, such as they are, taking a realistic view of that.
sentences.zh: 因此，我希望我们能从中吸取的教训是，你必须依靠人们的价值观（不管它们是什么样），并对此采取现实的看法。

sentences.en: That's the first point.
sentences.zh: 这是第一点。

sentences.en: The second point is, oh, guess what?
sentences.zh: 第二点是，哦，你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: People aren't entirely selfish.
sentences.zh: 人们并不完全是自私的。

sentences.en: Economists have to learn that lesson, too.
sentences.zh: 经济学家也必须吸取这个教训。

sentences.en: People are not entirely selfish.
sentences.zh: 人们并非完全自私。

sentences.en: We actually care a lot about others.
sentences.zh: 我们其实非常关心他人。

sentences.en: And the third is a little bit frightening.
sentences.zh: 第三点则有点可怕。

sentences.en: Yes, we care about others, and sometimes we care negatively.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们关心他人，有时我们抱持的是负面的关心。

sentences.en: So, for example, there have been reported increases in attacks on people of Asian descent in the course of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 例如，据报道，在大流行期间，针对亚裔的袭击事件有所增加。

sentences.en: And the rise of xenophobia in public statements and so on is just another reminder that one of the ways that we care about each other is that we care about their well-being,
sentences.zh: 公开言论中仇外心理的抬头等，只是又一次提醒我们，我们关心彼此的方式之一是关心他们的福祉，

sentences.en: we love them, and we're willing to sacrifice for them.
sentences.zh: 我们爱他们，我们愿意为他们做出牺牲。

sentences.en: We also sometimes despise them and are willing to treat them badly.
sentences.zh: 但有时我们也会鄙视他们，并愿意对他们恶语相向或恶劣对待。

sentences.en: So, then I think we have to face up to the fact that a lot of these values that we have, our susceptibility to kindness and cooperation,
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为我们必须正视这样一个事实：我们的许多价值观——我们对善良和合作的易感性，

sentences.en: comes along in the same package with a susceptibility to zealotry and hatred of outsiders.
sentences.zh: 与对狂热和仇视外来者的易感性是打包在一起的。

sentences.en: That's a real challenge for us in terms of thinking about how we can essentially have the better part of that without having the worse.
sentences.zh: 对于我们而言，真正的挑战在于思考如何才能基本上保留其好的一面，而剔除坏的一面。

sentences.en: I'm thinking that COVID-19, along with climate change, could be the driver of a new change, a change in both the economics, the content, and what we teach our students,
sentences.zh: 我在想，新冠肺炎疫情与气候变化一起，可能会成为变革的新驱动力，这种变革既包括经济学、内容以及我们教给学生的东西，

sentences.en: and also how we talk about the economy and how we talk about our futures.
sentences.zh: 也包括我们如何谈论经济以及我们如何谈论未来。

sentences.en: And if I'm right, it'll involve words like community, solidarity, and not just self-interest in markets and obedience to governments.
sentences.zh: 如果我没猜错的话，它将涉及社区、团结等词汇，而不仅仅是市场中的自利和对政府的服从。

sentences.en: Sam Bowles is a behavioral economist at the Santa Fe Institute.
sentences.zh: 萨姆·鲍尔斯是圣菲研究所的行为经济学家。

sentences.en: He is the author of The Moral Economy, Why Good Incentives Are No Substitute for Good Citizens.
sentences.zh: 他是《道德经济：为什么好的激励不能取代好的公民》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Sam, thank you for joining me today on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 萨姆，谢谢你今天来到“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: Thanks a lot.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I enjoyed the program.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢这个节目。

sentences.zh: “隐藏的大脑”由“隐藏的大脑”传媒制作。

sentences.en: For our Unsung Hero today, we thought we'd turn the mic over to a listener and bring you one of the stories from our sister podcast, My Unsung Hero.
sentences.zh: 对于今天的“无名英雄”，我们决定把麦克风交给我们的一位听众，为您带来我们的姊妹播客《我的无名英雄》中的一个故事。

sentences.en: A few years before college, Julie Ort suffered a major spinal cord injury.
sentences.zh: 上大学前几年，朱莉·奥特遭受了严重的脊髓损伤。

sentences.en: She was still recovering when she arrived on campus, which meant she had to walk with a leg brace and orthopedic crutches.
sentences.zh: 她到达校园时仍在康复中，这意味着她必须戴着腿部支具和矫形拐杖走路。

sentences.en: One day, early on in her freshman year, she was late to her physics class.
sentences.zh: 大一刚开学的一天，她上物理课迟到了。

sentences.en: It was in a large lecture hall with stadium seating, so everyone could see her as she awkwardly made her way up the stairs.
sentences.zh: 教室是一个带有阶梯座位的阶梯大教室，因此当她笨拙地走上楼梯时，每个人都能看到她。

sentences.en: I was carrying most of my books for the day because I was too slow to make it back to my dorm room in between classes.
sentences.zh: 我当时带着一天的大部分书，因为我走得太慢，课间没法赶回宿舍。

sentences.en: And I had a seat, five seats in on the second row and just figured I'd sit there, that it would put me close enough to kind of blend in.
sentences.zh: 我在第二排靠里面第五个座位有个座位，我想着就在那儿坐下，这样离得够近，还能融入进去。

sentences.en: But as I was scooting sideways between the first and second rows, that's when all of the laws of inertia, momentum, decided to conspire against me.
sentences.zh: 但就在我侧着身子在第一排和第二排之间挪动时，所有的惯性和动量定律决定联合起来与我作对。

sentences.en: My backpack shifted and I began to free fall backwards.
sentences.zh: 我的背包移位了，我开始向后自由落体。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, my legs shot straight up in the air so that the entire class was framed between my knees as they, in unison, gasped,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我的双腿笔直地朝空中飞去，整堂课的人都被框在我的膝盖中间，他们齐声倒吸了一口气，

sentences.en: some of them reaching their hands out as if they might be able to catch me, all of them with a look of absolute horror.
sentences.zh: 有些人伸出双手，好像能接住我一样，所有人都带着绝对惊恐的表情。

sentences.en: So I just said, it's okay, I'm not hurt, I'm fine, I guess I'll just sit here.
sentences.zh: 于是我脱口而出：“没关系，我没受伤，我很好，我想我就坐这儿吧。”

sentences.en: And mercifully, they laughed.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，他们笑了。

sentences.en: The instructor actually had to come over and help lift my legs over the back of the seat and swing me around to the front.
sentences.zh: 讲师甚至不得不走过来，帮我把双腿抬过座位靠背，把我转到前面。

sentences.en: And all the while, I just looked at him and begged, please, please, just go on teaching.
sentences.zh: 而在这期间，我只是看着他，恳求道：“求求你，求求你，继续讲课吧。”

sentences.en: The rest of the day was a blur.
sentences.zh: 那天剩下的时间里，一切都模模糊糊。

sentences.en: I couldn't look anyone in the eye.
sentences.zh: 我不敢直视任何人的眼睛。

sentences.en: I just kept thinking that for the next four years, I would meet people and never know if they might have been in that class.
sentences.zh: 我脑子里一直想着，在未来四年里，我会遇到各种各样的人，却永远不知道他们是否曾在那堂课上。

sentences.en: So that night, I decided to hide in the library in the back.
sentences.zh: 所以那天晚上，我决定躲在图书馆的最里边。

sentences.en: I found one of those study carols where you have two desks that are facing each other, but there's this high wooden partition in between them.
sentences.zh: 我找到了那种自习隔间，两张书桌面对面，中间有一块高高的木制隔板。

sentences.en: And I just kept my head down, reliving those god-awful 50 minutes of class where I sat there with a wall of pity to my back.
sentences.zh: 我一直低着头，脑海里不断重播那该死的50分钟课，当时我背对着一堵同情的墙。

sentences.en: There just seemed to be no way to recover from my embarrassment and shame.
sentences.zh: 看起来根本没有办法从尴尬和羞耻中走出来。

sentences.en: But at some point, I looked up to see a hand.
sentences.zh: 但在某个时刻，我抬头看到了一只手。

sentences.en: Just a hand, not a person.
sentences.zh: 只是一只手，不是一个人。

sentences.en: Slide two warm chocolate chip cookies across the desk toward me.
sentences.zh: 把两块温热的巧克力曲奇饼干顺着桌子滑向我。

sentences.en: So I leaned to my far right to see if maybe there was someone on the other side of the partition.
sentences.zh: 所以我向右侧探出身体，想看看隔板的另一边是不是有人。

sentences.en: And there was.
sentences.zh: 还真有。

sentences.en: It was another student.
sentences.zh: 是另一个学生。

sentences.en: And he leaned out to meet my gaze and just shrugged and said,
sentences.zh: 他探出身来迎着我的目光，耸了耸肩说：

sentences.en: I was in physics class today.
sentences.zh: 我今天也上物理课了。

sentences.en: That was it.
sentences.zh: 就这些。

sentences.en: And then I ate those warm chocolate chip cookies.
sentences.zh: 然后我吃掉了那些温热的巧克力曲奇饼干。

sentences.en: I often say that there's a fine line between humiliation and humility.
sentences.zh: 我常说，羞辱与谦逊之间只有一线之隔。

sentences.en: To my unsung hero, I want you to know that what to you might have felt like an act of compassion,
sentences.zh: 致我的无名英雄，我想让你知道，对你来说可能只是出于同情的一个举动，

sentences.en: a moment of meeting me in my grief, was something that changed me.
sentences.zh: 在我悲伤时给予我的一刻陪伴，却改变了我。

sentences.en: It made me realize that even in those moments of being brought incredibly low,
sentences.zh: 它让我意识到，即使在跌入人生低谷的时刻，

sentences.en: there are people who just want you to take that next step forward.
sentences.zh: 也总有人只希望你迈出向前的那一步。

sentences.en: And that's what I did.
sentences.zh: 而我确实这样做了。

sentences.en: For you and for me.
sentences.zh: 为了你，也为了我。

sentences.en: I don't remember your face.
sentences.zh: 我不记得你的脸。

sentences.en: I didn't think to ask your name.
sentences.zh: 我没想到去问你的名字。

sentences.en: But I have never forgotten your kindness.
sentences.zh: 但我从未忘记你的善良。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Julie Ort of Highlands Ranch, Colorado.
sentences.zh: 朱莉·奥特，来自科罗拉多州高地牧场。

sentences.en: She says it took about 10 years to recover from her spinal injury,
sentences.zh: 她说她花了大约 10 年时间才从脊髓损伤中恢复过来，

sentences.en: and she still walks with a cane.
sentences.zh: 现在她走路仍需拄着手杖。

sentences.en: But today, she's a passionate biker and a cross-country skier.
sentences.zh: 但如今，她是一位狂热的骑行爱好者和越野滑雪者。

sentences.en: You can share your unsung hero with us.
sentences.zh: 你可以与我们分享你的无名英雄的故事。

sentences.en: Record a voice memo on your phone and send it to myunsunghero at hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 在手机上录一段语音备忘录，并发送至 myunsunghero@hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.zh: 下周，我们将为你带来“读心术 2.0”系列的最终集。

sentences.en: It examines the way we communicate and miscommunicate with our loved ones.
sentences.zh: 它探讨了我们与所爱之人沟通和沟通不畅的方式。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: See you soon.
sentences.zh: 再见。
